summary: Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and Goethe University Frankfurt, earning his doctorate under Paul Thieme. He served as an assistant at the University of Göttingen before holding a full professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and his habilitation at Leipzig University. He lectured in Sanskrit philology at Leipzig (1970–1991) and taught at Frankfurt, Bayreuth, and Göttingen.
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen, working under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain, and served as professor of Turkology at Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. His posts include positions at the University of Göttingen (attested 1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA under Klaus Sagaster, a PhD at Marburg under Michael Hahn, and a habilitation at Hamburg, later serving as director of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and professor at Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a theology diploma at Benediktbeuern, obtained a doctorate in theology at the University of Munich, and later served there as a lecturer in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Uppsala University under the supervision of Peter Schalk in 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He was appointed professor in the history of religions at the University of Bergen in 1996.

Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and taught at Naropa University in 2001.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president in 1909, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1963 to 1999.
Kodo Nomura was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He later served as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Takada Junior College, Senju-ji, and Hōryūji Kangakuin, studying under Sotan Oka and others. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned an MA at KU Leuven and studied at Banaras Hindu University between ~1988 and 1992.

Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who received a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Komazawa University, serving as Komazawa's president in 1976.

Kogi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and worked as an editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn and earned his PhD at Kyushu University. He was a professor at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991, 1997–2000).
